html:
Optional redaction and literal execution

agent_runtime/redaction.py owns optional credential classification and masking for runtime consumer projections. Optional redaction cannot authorize, reject, retry, repair, or change an operation. Canonical messages, arguments, HTTP profiles, files, receipts, working context, cache evidence and resume data retain literal values.

Settings → Redaction exposes 20 independent switches. New installations start with every switch on. Existing saved choices and accepted run snapshots are preserved; missing preferences in older stores retain their historical off fallback. The persisted key is redaction_<source>_enabled. Enable all and Disable all use the existing settings autosave without confirmation.

Source Consumer Policy lifetime

tool_output Generic result previews Run snapshot

audit Audit details Live
schedules Schedule inspection Live

working_context Working-context model projection Run snapshot

database Database result previews Run snapshot

New runs freeze the ten run sources in redaction_policy. Queue, continuation and restart carry that snapshot. Diagnostic sources read the existing UI settings store. Gateway calls carry a validated, stripped policy envelope; it is never a domain tool argument. Omitted fields in a policy mapping mean off, and values must be actual booleans. This compatibility fallback is distinct from loading an existing current run: bind_run_mode rejects a loaded state without redaction_policy rather than silently adopting newer settings.

The processor's off path returns the original object or stream fragment immediately. It does not evaluate a lazy credential context, traverse/copy the value, compile patterns, parse URLs, buffer or reserialize text. Policy resolution still reads the settings owner unless a response projection scope already holds that snapshot. Compatibility discovery helpers are gated by whether any optional source is on; callers should keep source-specific discovery lazy. Size limits, structural reasoning exclusions and transport framing remain separate.

Public error diagnostics have a separate mandatory boundary in error_catalog/redaction.py: bounded, cycle-safe sanitization applies even when optional error projection is off. error_catalog/compatibility.py also marks catalog variables declared nonpublic. OAuth callback logging in native/http_oauth.py always strips callback query strings before applying optional log projection. These boundaries protect diagnostic and protocol output; they do not replace authoritative operation arguments or receipts. The diagnostic pipeline explains mandatory sanitization, occurrence identity, bounded HTTP enrichment and generated help separately from optional evidence projection. Recipe capture uses the central processor to detect values that cannot be retained in reusable workflow definitions.

On produces detached projections. Sensitive fields are exact names, not substrings such as key inside monkey. Known materials carry provenance and one of field-only, exact-scalar, substring or encoded-substring matching. Sensitive-record metadata masks that record's projection without promoting every scalar into global secrets. Matching is longest-first with an opaque [redacted] marker; projection is idempotent. The processor recognizes credential assignments, authentication headers, private keys, URL userinfo and sensitive query fields. Streaming uses bounded holdback and consumes long credential tokens without retaining their body. An oversized uninterrupted URL may be represented by one marker. No redaction path calls an LLM.

Projection ownership and limits

flowchart LR Raw[Canonical messages / arguments / receipts] --> Consumer[Consumer chooses one source] Saved[Accepted run policy] --> Policy[Effective policy] Live[Live diagnostic settings] --> Policy Policy --> Consumer Consumer --> Enabled{Source enabled?} Enabled -->|No| Identity[Original value or fragment] Enabled -->|Yes| Context[Lazy explicit credential context] Context --> Mask[Central matcher / stream] Identity --> Sink[Consumer-specific view] Mask --> Sink Sink --> Bounds[Independent display limits and mandatory error privacy]

Projection scopes snapshot live settings once per response or batch and reuse that value for nested projections. A nested run policy can still change the ten accepted-run sources. Scopes restore their ContextVars on exit and must not span an SSE wait or generator yield. The immutable matcher cache is separate: it retains at most 128 contexts, their explicit secret materials and compiled patterns in process memory, without time-based expiry.

The optional walker copies supported mappings, lists and tuples; sensitive-record metadata masks scalar leaves without promoting them to global substring secrets. It assumes acyclic supported input and has no cycle or depth guard. Undecodable bytes and unfamiliar object types pass through. JSON object/array strings can be parsed and reserialized when masking is enabled, so even a readable projection is not an exact-byte substitute for canonical content. Caller-supplied field names must use the normalized spelling; query-name matching uses decoded names.

Enabled streams capture policy when created. Their ordinary holdback is based on max(8192, longest explicit secret variant) characters, and they initially buffer up to twice that amount before emitting. Long recognized tokens use a delimiter discard state; very large fragments can still allocate before trimming. Final flush is required to emit pending text. These are streaming matcher limits, not a universal byte cap or a mechanism for rejecting provider output.

For retained job-log pages, known-secret suffix/prefix fragments at page edges can be masked conservatively even when the complete credential is absent from the page. This affects only the consumer text; absolute cursors and raw retained bytes remain unchanged.

Consumer projection selects one source from capability/receipt identity before masking. It restores declared receipt status and execution-control fields from the original object, and handles text represented as base64 File content without rewriting source offsets. Public run snapshots copy wait/reasoning control identities independently. These protections keep masking from turning an execution fact into a different result.

Observability projection applies size and telemetry-shape checks separately from optional redaction. Standard values use 1,000-character strings, 20 list items and depth 4; strict values use 400, 10 and 3. Debug values use 10,000,000 characters, 100,000 list items and depth 32. Truncation markers add to the retained prefix, dictionaries have no item-count cap, and selected telemetry fields follow their own validation branches. These are per-value limits, not an aggregate serialized-byte budget. Execution event families use debug limits for details while summaries retain ordinary limits. Mandatory public-error handling still applies when optional trace redaction is off.

Gateway policy transport replaces reserved metadata from authenticated controller context and strips it from the mutable incoming payload before domain execution. A Gateway without a live settings reader uses that bound policy for the operation. Disabled-check observations are a separate channel capped at 16 records and 8,192 ASCII JSON characters; they do not alter tool arguments or execution outcomes.

The processor fixtures, execution-invariance fixtures and response-scope fixtures exercise source isolation, unchanged literal HTTP results, exact disabled identity, stream boundaries and nested/concurrent policy ownership using local data and services.

Authentication

Literal credentials are accepted in ordinary chat and tool arguments. Missing values use ordinary ask_user interaction. HTTP v3 profiles store values inside auth: username/password, token, API-key value, literal session login fields and header-rule value. OAuth accepts literal client/access/refresh tokens. TLS accepts PEM values or Gateway paths; proxy authentication uses literal username/password. Sudo uses sudo_password and optional sudo_username. Values can appear in logs, model content and UI when their owning switch is off.

Secure Prompts, its Agent Check, ingress/egress blockers and volatile password vault are retired. Current guard/configuration boundaries reject unsupported fields. HTTP profiles require v3 literal values; private credential maps and slot references are unsupported. Pre-baseline credential waits are not converted. Already-redacted values cannot be reconstructed.

OAuth browser/device interaction remains a protocol feature using waiting_user. State, PKCE, callback identity, expiry and single-use code handling remain enforced. TLS verification, Gateway identity, capability/permission policy, resource limits, origin rules and execution truth remain owned by their existing subsystems.

Source map and contributor rule

  • redaction.py: policy, provenance, matching, streams and logging adapters.
  • native/redaction_policy.py: admission and resume snapshots.
  • native/consumer_projection.py: model/UI source selection.
  • observability/projection.py: independent size bounds and sink projection.
  • gateway_core/runtime_policy.py: transport policy envelope.
  • gateway_core/http_profiles.py: strict current literal-profile validation.
  • native/http_session_state.py: OAuth interaction and HTTP session lifecycle.
  • api/agent_ui_support/route_groups/settings.py: settings registry.
  • api/static/agent_ui/settings.js: switches and bulk controls.

New code must not implement credential masking locally. Add a new RedactionSource only when a genuinely new first-class projection sink cannot map to an existing source, and use the canonical processor. Never persist a projected value as canonical execution, recovery or completion evidence.

Credential-interaction cleanup does not change the twenty independent Redaction sources or the user's choices. Literal authentication input is ordinary text. Configured consumers may project it through the existing central processor, while canonical arguments, execution values and raw receipts remain authoritative. http.connect.auth_values overrides only advertised authentication leaves on a copy of a saved profile; it does not save the reply to Parameter Store.

When Model input redaction is enabled, matched values supplied in chat—including credentials—may be hidden from the Agent model on new runs. Authentication tasks that require the Agent to reuse a value from the conversation may therefore require Model input redaction to remain off. The choice remains yours; no special input form or automatic bypass is introduced.

Proxmox accepts invocation-local auth_values for username/password. Database accepts user/password; host/port/dbname remain configured profile identity. Both use ordinary ask_user and never automatically save transient authentication.

Clipboard, Screen, Browser and UI tools omit transient device payloads from diagnostics and portable history independently of credential redaction switches. Diagnostics identify these tools from structured invocation metadata, not filenames, command text, documentation or tool catalogs. For example, reading auth/browser.py does not activate device-content filtering. Actual device tool use still filters subsequent diagnostics that could repeat the observed content, while exact source receipts remain unchanged; see Current clipboard. This does not add a redaction setting or secret classifier.

Google Workspace and legacy Gmail OAuth authority have an unconditional structural privacy boundary in auth/privacy.py, independent of these optional redaction switches. The google_oauth_app / google_account families join the existing protected OAuth families: accepted references and public Parameter projections contain only safe identity and scope metadata. Shared browser callbacks suppress access-log query strings, and provider errors expose catalog codes rather than token response bodies. Handshake state, ID tokens and PKCE verifiers remain private ephemeral runtime data. No new redaction switch, vault or masking engine is introduced.
